stem: Butan-1-ol (b.p. 390 K) boils at a higher temperature than butan-1-amine (b.p. 351 K) although their molar masses are almost equal. Why?

stem: Why is aniline a weaker base than ammonia?

Its nitrogen lone pair is delocalised over the ring
Its anilinium ion has five resonance structures

stem: Acylation of an amine with an acid chloride is carried out in the presence of pyridine. What is the role of pyridine?

stem: Which sequence gives p-bromoaniline as the major product from aniline?

(CH3CO)2O; then Br2 in CH3COOH; then H3O+
NaNO2/HCl at 273 K; then H3PO2; then Br2(aq)
explanation: Correct option: (A). Bromine water gives 2,4,6-tribromoaniline, the -NH2 group placing the three bromines meta to each other. Diazotisation and then reduction with H3PO2 replace the diazonium group by H, leaving 1,3,5-tribromobenzene. Starting with Sandmeyer gives bromobenzene, which brominates at ortho/para; the acetylation route gives p-bromoaniline; and removing nitrogen first leaves benzene, which is not tribrominated meta by bromine water.
